interactions.label: Which public health emergency was declared a Public Health Emergency of Internat

params.question: Which public health emergency was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) by the WHO on two separate occasions — in July 2022 and again in August 2024?

answers.text: COVID-19

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: COVID-19 was declared a PHEIC once, on 30th January 2020, and subsequently a pandemic on 11th March 2020. It was not declared a PHEIC on two separate occasions.

answers.text: Nipah virus infection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nipah caused outbreaks in Kerala in 2018 and 2023 with very high case fatality rates, but it remained geographically limited and was not declared a PHEIC.

answers.text: Mpox

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mpox (formerly monkeypox) was declared a PHEIC twice: first during a multi-country outbreak in July 2022, and again in August 2024 after a more severe strain emerged in Africa — a distinction unique among recent health emergencies.

answers.text: H5N1 avian influenza

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: H5N1 re-emerged in cattle in the United States in 2024, raising pandemic preparedness concerns, but it was not declared a PHEIC on two occasions.

overallFeedback.feedback: Incorrect. Mpox was declared a PHEIC twice — first in July 2022 during a multi-country outbreak and again in August 2024 when a more severe strain emerged in Africa.
Correct! Mpox is the only recent health emergency to have been declared a PHEIC twice by the WHO, reflecting the evolving and unpredictable nature of the threat.

interactions.label: Antimicrobial resistance is primarily driven by the overuse of antibiotics in hu

params.question: Antimicrobial resistance is primarily driven by the overuse of antibiotics in humans and has no significant connection to antibiotic use in farm animals.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The video explains that overuse of antibiotics in both humans and farm animals drives antimicrobial resistance. Agricultural antibiotic use is a major contributor — this is a core example of the One Health framework's principle that human, animal, and environmental health are inextricably linked.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The narration states that overuse of antibiotics in both people and farm animals drives AMR. Agricultural antibiotic use contributes significantly to the emergence and spread of resistant organisms, reinforcing the One Health principle that human, animal, and environmental health are interconnected.

params.question: During an active outbreak, you observe that the effective reproduction number (Rt) has dropped from 2.5 to 0.8 over two weeks. What does this change indicate about the trajectory of the outbreak?

answers.text: The outbreak is accelerating and stricter containment measures are urgently needed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An Rt of 0.8 is below 1.0, meaning the outbreak is not accelerating. When Rt was 2.5, each case was generating 2.5 new infections; now it is producing fewer than one.

answers.text: Each case is now generating fewer than one new infection, indicating the outbreak is declining

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: When Rt drops below 1.0, each existing case produces, on average, fewer than one new infection, so the outbreak is shrinking. During COVID-19, district-level Rt values guided local restriction decisions in India.

answers.text: The case fatality rate has improved due to better treatment protocols

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rt measures transmission dynamics, not treatment outcomes. The case fatality rate (CFR) is a separate metric reflecting the proportion of confirmed cases that die.

answers.text: Herd immunity has been achieved and the vaccination campaign can be discontinued

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An Rt below 1 does not necessarily mean herd immunity has been reached. Containment measures, behavioural changes, and partial vaccination all contribute. Stopping vaccination prematurely can trigger a rebound.

overallFeedback.feedback: Incorrect. When Rt falls below 1, the outbreak is declining because each case is generating, on average, fewer than one new infection. This was a key metric for COVID-19 decision-making.
Correct! Rt below 1 signals that the outbreak is declining — a critical metric that guided real-time public health decisions during COVID-19 in India.

interactions.label: The 1995 Supreme Court judgement in IMA versus V.P. Shantha had which major cons

params.question: The 1995 Supreme Court judgement in IMA versus V.P. Shantha had which major consequence for medical practice in India?

answers.text: It classified medical services as a 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act, enabling patients to file negligence claims in consumer forums

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This landmark ruling held that medical care counts as a 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act, allowing patients to seek compensation through civil consumer forums without going through criminal courts — leading to a massive rise in medical negligence cases.

answers.text: It established the National Medical Commission as the apex regulatory body for doctors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The NMC was established much later by the NMC Act of 2019 (enacted 2020), replacing the Indian Medical Council. This 1995 judgement dealt with consumer protection, not professional regulation.

answers.text: It mandated professional indemnity insurance for all practising physicians in India

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While indemnity insurance is advisable, this judgement did not mandate it. The ruling specifically addressed whether medical services fall under consumer protection law.

answers.text: It introduced criminal penalties of up to seven years for attacks on healthcare workers

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Protection of healthcare workers from violence was addressed later, in the 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, which made such attacks punishable with up to seven years' imprisonment.

overallFeedback.feedback: Incorrect. The IMA vs V.P. Shantha ruling classified medical services as a 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act, allowing patients to file negligence claims in consumer forums without criminal proceedings.
Correct! This landmark 1995 ruling opened consumer forums as a route for medical negligence claims, fundamentally transforming the medico-legal environment for Indian doctors.

interactions.label: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, up to how many weeks of ge

params.question: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, up to how many weeks of gestation can a pregnancy be terminated with the opinion of a single registered medical practitioner?

answers.text: 12 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The earlier version of the MTP Act had a 12-week threshold for a single doctor's opinion, but the amended Act extends this limit to 20 weeks.

answers.text: 20 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The MTP Act permits termination up to 20 weeks with one doctor's opinion. For special categories, two doctors' opinions are needed up to 24 weeks, and beyond 24 weeks, only a medical board can approve termination.

answers.text: 24 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 24 weeks is the upper limit for special categories under the MTP Act, and it requires two doctors' opinions — not one. A single doctor's opinion suffices only up to 20 weeks.

answers.text: 28 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 28 weeks is not a threshold specified in the MTP Act. Termination beyond 24 weeks requires medical board approval regardless of the indication.

overallFeedback.feedback: Incorrect. Under the MTP Act, a single registered medical practitioner can approve termination up to 20 weeks of gestation.
Correct! The MTP Act specifies a tiered system: one doctor up to 20 weeks, two doctors for special categories up to 24 weeks, and a medical board beyond that.

params.question: A patient files a medical negligence complaint against a community physician in a consumer forum. The court applies the Bolam test to evaluate the case. What does the Bolam test require the physician to demonstrate?

answers.text: That informed consent was documented in writing before the clinical procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While documenting consent is essential for defending against negligence claims, the Bolam test specifically evaluates the standard of clinical care provided, not the consent process itself.

answers.text: That the treatment outcome fell within statistically expected complication rates

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Bolam test does not rely on statistical outcome rates. It evaluates whether the doctor's clinical decisions were consistent with a practice accepted by a responsible body of medical professionals.

answers.text: That the care provided was consistent with what a responsible body of medical professionals would consider acceptable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Bolam principle holds that a doctor is not negligent if they acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of medical opinion — the standard applied in consumer forums for medical negligence cases in India.

answers.text: That the physician held valid registration with the State Medical Council at the time of treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Valid registration is a prerequisite for legal practice, but it is not the test for whether care was negligent. The Bolam test specifically assesses whether the clinical standard of care met the threshold accepted by responsible professionals.

overallFeedback.feedback: Incorrect. The Bolam test asks whether the care provided was consistent with what a responsible body of medical professionals would consider acceptable practice.

Correct! The Bolam principle tests whether the physician's care met the standard that a responsible body of medical professionals would endorse — the key legal test in consumer forum negligence cases.
